misconceptions.description: Believing that duplicating narration as identical on-screen text gives learners more access and is therefore safer.
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds on-screen text identical to the narration to be thorough
misconceptions.feedback: Identical on-screen text plus narration overloads the visual channel and forces reconciliation. For novices, keep the graphic plus narration and drop the duplicated text.

misconceptions.description: Assuming that interesting extras such as background video, music, or decorative images raise learning because they raise engagement.
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds engaging-but-extraneous media to motivate learners
misconceptions.feedback: The coherence principle: extraneous material competes for limited capacity. Remove or minimize seductive details and justify any retained media by the learning goal.

misconceptions.description: Treating Mayer's principles as universal rules that apply identically to every learner, ignoring expertise reversal and pacing conditions.
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies a principle without naming the target learner or conditions
misconceptions.feedback: State the principle as a constraint with boundary conditions. Name the target learner, prior knowledge, and pacing before applying it, since some effects reverse for experts.
